text:
Maya Chen: Hey all, trying to accept the GitHub org invite but it keeps redirecting me to my personal account (I have two). When I click the invite link it asks me to 'claim your account' and then shows no repos. Anyone seen this flow before?

Alex Rivera: Hi Maya - welcome! Which email did you use for the invite? sometimes GH ties invites to the invite email.

Maya Chen: I used my work email (maya@redwood.ai) - I can sign into GH with that, but the invite page shows my personal GH username at the top and a button to switch accounts. If I switch to the work account, it says "You must enable SSO to access this organization".

Samir Patel: @Maya Chen that SSO prompt is expected for org members. Did you accept the SSO authorization after signing into your work account? There should be a blue button on the org page to authorize SAML/SSO.

Maya Chen: I clicked authorize but then I get a 403 when trying to view private repos - the invite page still lists 0 repos. Also my profile shows "Outside collaborator" in the org banner.

Alex Rivera: Hmm. Sounds like the invite might be linked to your personal account (email collision). Two quick checks: 1) Can you open https://github.com/organizations/redwood-inference/settings/people and search your work email? 2) Do you see the invite in https://github.com/notifications or https://github.com/settings/organizations?

Maya Chen: I can see the invite under Notifications but when I accept it the org still shows me as outside collaborator.

Onboarding Bot: Your onboarding checklist has been updated: GitHub invite accepted (pending org membership sync).

Luke (DevEx): Hi Maya - I can fix this from our side. Two options: (A) If your personal GH account has your work email, we can transfer the invite to the correct account; (B) we can remove the personal account from the invite and resend to maya@redwood.ai. Which do you prefer?

Maya Chen: Prefer (B) - my personal account is old and I don't want it mixed.

Samir Patel: Before we reissue, confirm you have 2FA enabled on the work account. Org policy requires 2FA. Go to https://github.com/settings/security and enable "Two-factor authentication" if not enabled.

Maya Chen: I enabled 2FA a minute ago (auth app).

Alex Rivera: Okay Maya, I removed the pending link to your personal account and resent the invite to maya@redwood.ai. You should get a new email; accept it while logged into the work account (or use an incognito window to avoid session cross-over).

Maya Chen: Got the new invite email - accepted! The org now shows me as a member and I can see the team repos. Thanks y'all. :tada:

Luke (DevEx): Awesome - welcome aboard! If you hit any repo permission oddities (push denied, can't see a private repo), ping #eng or DM me and I'll check team mappings.

Maya Chen: Small follow-up: my ssh keys aren't present on the account after the transfer. Any tips?

Samir Patel: Add your public key to https://github.com/settings/keys and then run `ssh -T git@github.com` to confirm. If you see "Hi maya! You've successfully authenticated" you're good.

Maya Chen: `ssh -T` worked. All set. Thanks again.

Alex Rivera: Welcome to Redwood, Maya :wave: If you need a quick tour of repo layout, ping me and I’ll share the starter PR checklist.
